title: Constant-time string comparison must encode to bytes first (secrets.compare_digest rejects non-ASCII str)
answers: comparing strings with non-ASCII characters is not supported
how to compare secrets in constant time in pydantic
SecretStr equality fails with unicode / emoji password
body:
Symptom: comparing two `SecretStr` values that contain non-ASCII characters (e.g. 'café') raises `TypeError: comparing strings with non-ASCII characters is not supported` instead of returning True/False.
Root cause: pydantic/types.py:SecretStr.__eq__ passed raw `str` values to `secrets.compare_digest()`. That function only accepts ASCII when given `str` arguments.
Fix pattern: encode both sides before comparing with `.encode('utf-8', errors='surrogatepass')`. The comparison stays constant-time and works for any str. `surrogatepass` is needed so that lone surrogates (e.g. '\ud800'), which strict utf-8 cannot encode, don't raise.
Constraints: this applies to every `compare_digest` call that takes `str`. `SecretBytes` needs no change because `compare_digest` accepts arbitrary bytes. Keep the `isinstance(other, self.__class__)` guard: a `SecretStr` must never equal a plain `str`. Tests are in tests/test_types.py:test_secretstr_equality, which covers non-ASCII values and lone surrogates.
applies: Equality/constant-time comparison of SecretStr and any secret str compared via secrets.compare_digest in pydantic/types.py
